facts.statement: Dinheirosaurus lourinhanensis was first described by José Bonaparte and Octávio Mateus in 1999 based on fossils from the Lourinhã Formation.
facts.quote: The only species is Dinheirosaurus lourinhanensis, first described by José Bonaparte and Octávio Mateus in 1999 for vertebrae and some other material from the Lourinhã Formation.

facts.statement: Dinheirosaurus lived during the early Tithonian stage of the Late Jurassic period.
facts.quote: Although the precise age of the formation is not known, it can be dated around the early Tithonian of the Late Jurassic.

facts.statement: Researchers have suggested that Dinheirosaurus might actually be a species of Supersaurus.
facts.quote: It may represent a species of Supersaurus.

facts.statement: The holotype specimen of Dinheirosaurus, catalogued as ML 414, was discovered in 1987 by Carlos Anunciação.
facts.quote: ML 414 was first uncovered in 1987 by Mr. Carlos Anunciação.

facts.statement: The name Dinheirosaurus lourinhanensis translates to "Porto Dinheiro lizard from Lourinhã".
facts.quote: This new species was described as Dinheirosaurus lourinhanensis, with a full meaning of "Porto Dinheiro lizard from Lourinhã".

facts.statement: Excavating the Dinheirosaurus fossils required heavy machinery, including a bulldozer and a tilt hammer.
facts.quote: To remove the fossils from the surrounding rock, a bulldozer and tilt hammer were needed.

facts.statement: Dinheirosaurus is estimated to have reached a length of 20 to 25 meters and weighed approximately 8.8 metric tons.
facts.quote: In total, Dinheirosaurus would have had an approximate length of 20 - 25 m and weighed 8.8 MT.

facts.statement: A 1.05-meter-long footprint found near Dinheirosaurus fossils suggests the genus may have been even larger than current estimates.
facts.quote: A giant footprint was found in the same locality as Dinheirosaurus. At 1.05 m in length it was considered as possibly coming from Dinheirosaurus and might indicate this genus could attain giant sizes.

facts.statement: Only two cervical vertebrae are preserved from the Dinheirosaurus holotype, despite the animal likely having fifteen.
facts.quote: Of the cervicals, only two of the assumed fifteen are preserved.

facts.statement: The preserved fourteenth cervical vertebra has a centrum length of 63 cm and is well-preserved with a concave bottom edge.
facts.quote: The length of the centrum is 71 cm, and the fourteenth cervical is quite similar overall. 63 cm is the total measurement of the 14th cervical's centrum, which is well-preserved, complete, and concave along the bottom edge.

facts.statement: The dorsal vertebrae of Dinheirosaurus vary in length, ranging from 58 cm for the first dorsal down to 25 cm for the seventh.
facts.quote: The dorsal vary in length from the 58 cm of the first dorsal to the 25 cm of the seventh, eight and ninth dorsals.

facts.statement: A 2012 study by Mannion et al. classified Dinheirosaurus as the sister species to Supersaurus vivianae, forming the most basal group of diplodocines.
facts.quote: In 2012 during a redescription of the taxon by Philip Mannion et al., it was recovered, in both cladograms, to be sister species to Supersaurus vivianae and together forming the most basal diplodocines.

facts.statement: In 2015, Dinheirosaurus lourinhanensis was reclassified as a species of Supersaurus, becoming Supersaurus lourinhanensis.
facts.quote: In 2015, Dinheirosaurus lourinhanensis was considered a species of Supersaurus in a new combination S. lourinhanensis

facts.statement: Dinheirosaurus likely possessed a whip-like tail, a characteristic feature of diplodocids.
facts.quote: As a diplodocid, it is probable that Dinheirosaurus possessed a whip-tail.

facts.statement: Due to its relationship with Apatosaurus and Diplodocus, Dinheirosaurus likely had a squared snout.
facts.quote: Being related to both Apatosaurus and Diplodocus, Dinheirosaurus probably possessed a squared snout.

facts.statement: Dinheirosaurus was likely a non-selective ground feeder.
facts.quote: This means that it was probably a non-selective ground-feeding sauropod.

facts.statement: A 2014 cladogram suggested that Dinheirosaurus was more primitive than Apatosaurus and placed it outside the subfamily Diplodocinae.
facts.quote: However, a cladogram from 2014 found that their group was supported, but in fact more primitive than Apatosaurus, and therefore outside Diplodocinae.

facts.statement: The hypothesis that Dinheirosaurus is a species of Supersaurus remains unconfirmed because further preparation of the holotype remains is needed.
facts.quote: However, to either confirm or refute this hypothesis, several remains of the holotype need to be prepared.

facts.statement: Dinheirosaurus is one of the few sauropods known to have gastroliths found alongside its type specimen.
facts.quote: Dinheirosaurus is one of relatively few sauropods for which gastroliths were found obviously alongside the type specimen.

facts.statement: Research suggests Dinheirosaurus likely used gastroliths to absorb minerals rather than for an avian-style gastric mill, as its gastrolith mass was far lower than the 1.05% typical of birds.
facts.quote: When birds were typically found to have 1.05% of their body weight gastroliths, the sauropod Diplodocus, which had the highest amount of gastroliths, only amassed to 0.03% body weight.

facts.statement: Dinheirosaurus lived in the Lourinhã Formation during the Late Jurassic.
facts.quote: Dinheirosaurus was one of many dinosaurs to have lived in the Lourinhã Formation during the Late Jurassic.

facts.statement: The Lourinhã Formation, where Dinheirosaurus lived, contained a fauna similar to the North American Morrison Formation, including many theropods, sauropods, and ornithischians.
facts.quote: Many theropods, sauropods, and especially ornithischians are also from the Lourinhã Formation, which contains a similar fauna to the North American Morrison Formation.

facts.statement: Dinheirosaurus is one of many eusauropods found in the Late Jurassic of Europe.
facts.quote: Many eusauropods, including Dinheirosaurus have been found in the Late Jurassic of Europe.

facts.statement: Dinheirosaurus lived around the base of the Tithonian stage, indicated by the presence of the fossil species Anchispirocyclina lusitanica.
facts.quote: The sauropods are from around the base of the Tithonian as based on the presence of Anchispirocyclina lusitanica.

facts.statement: The genus Supersaurus, which includes the species lourinhanensis formerly known as Dinheirosaurus, was named by Bonaparte and Mateus in 1999.
facts.quote: genus_authority: Bonaparte & Mateus, 1999

facts.statement: The species lourinhanensis was described by Tschopp and colleagues.
facts.quote: species_authority: Tschopp et al.

facts.statement: Dinheirosaurus lived approximately 156 million years ago during the Kimmeridgian stage of the Late Jurassic in what is now Europe.
facts.quote: que vivió a finales del período Jurásico, hace aproximadamente 156 millones de años, en el Kimmeridgiense, en lo que es hoy Europa.

facts.statement: Dinheirosaurus evolved from a primitive diplodocid distinct from Diplodocus in an isolated environment because the Iberian Peninsula was an island at that time.
facts.quote: Supersaurus lourinhanensis evolucionó de un diplodócido más primitivo que el Diplodocus en un ambiente separado ya que la península ibérica era una isla en esa época.

facts.statement: Dinheirosaurus lourinhanensis is estimated to have reached a length of approximately 25 meters.
facts.quote: En total, Supersaurus lourinhanensis habría tenido una longitud aproximada de 25 metros.

facts.statement: The known remains of Dinheirosaurus consist mainly of partial ribs and a fragment of the pelvis, with little non-vertebral material.
facts.quote: El animal no se conoce bien a partir de material no vertebral, actualmente solo consiste en costillas parciales y un fragmento de pelvis.

facts.statement: Non-vertebral appendicular material includes a very incomplete and fragmentary pubis and more than one hundred gastroliths.
facts.quote: Otro material apendicular, no vertebral, incluye un eje muy incompleto y fragmentario del pubis, y más de cien gastrolitos.

facts.statement: Only two of the fifteen presumed cervical vertebrae of Dinheirosaurus have been preserved.
facts.quote: De las cervicales, solo dos de los quince supuestos se conservan.

facts.statement: The dorsal vertebrae of Dinheirosaurus vary in length from 58 centimeters for the first dorsal to 25 centimeters for the seventh, eighth, and ninth dorsals.
facts.quote: La longitud dorsal varía desde los 58 centímetros de la primera dorsal hasta los 25 centímetros de la séptima, octava y novena dorsales.

facts.statement: The height of the dorsal vertebrae varies significantly, ranging from a low of 51 centimeters to a high of 76 centimeters starting from the first dorsal.
facts.quote: La altura en las vértebras también es bastante variable, con una altura más baja de 51 centímetro de altura a 76 centímetro de altura aumentando desde la primera dorsal.

facts.statement: The holotype specimen of Dinheirosaurus was discovered in 1987 by Mr. Carlos Anunciação.
facts.quote: El ejemplar holotipo se descubrió en 1987 por el Sr. Carlos Anunciação.

facts.statement: Excavations at the discovery site lasted from 1987 until 1992, after which the specimen was moved to the Lourinhã Museum and cataloged as ML 414.
facts.quote: El ejemplar holotipo se descubrió en 1987 por el Sr. Carlos Anunciação. Fue comunicado al Museo de Lourinhã, y después de las excavaciones que duraron desde el momento del descubrimiento hasta 1992, el espécimen se trasladó al museo y se catalogó con el número ML 414.

facts.statement: A preliminary report on the holotype (ML 414) was published by Dantas et al. immediately after the excavations were completed.
facts.quote: Dantas et al. realizó un informe preliminar de ML 414 tan pronto como las excavaciones estuvieron completas.

facts.statement: The species was formally described as Dinheirosaurus lourinhanensis, meaning "Lizard of Porto Dinheiro, Lourinhã".
facts.quote: Esta nueva especie fue descrita como Dinheirosaurus lourinhanensis, con el significado completo de " Lagarto de Porto Dinheiro, Lourinhã ".

facts.statement: David Weishampel et al. disagreed with the identification of all material as Dinheirosaurus, finding only 9 dorsal vertebrae in the holotype and misinterpreting the pubis as a limb fragment.
facts.quote: David Weishampel et al. no reconoció todo el material como perteneciente a Dinheirosaurus y solo encontró 9 dorsales en el holotipo, mientras que también malinterpreta el pubis como un fragmento de extremidad.

facts.statement: A second set of vertebrae, collection number ML 418, was originally assigned to Dinheirosaurus but is now considered an unidentified new genus of diplodocid.
facts.quote: Otro par de vértebras, bajo el número de colección ML 418, fue asignado originalmente a Dinheirosaurus por Bonaparte y Mateus, pero ahora se considera que es un nuevo género no identificado de diplodócido.

facts.statement: In 2015, Tschopp et al. reclassified Dinheirosaurus lourinhanensis as a species of Supersaurus under the new combination Supersaurus lourinhanensis.
facts.quote: En 2015, en el trabajo de Tschopp et al. Dinheirosaurus lourinhanensis fue considerada una especie de Supersaurus bajo una nueva combinación Supersaurus lourinhanensis.

facts.statement: In 2012, Philip Mannion et al. redescribed the taxon as the sister species of Supersaurus vivianae, together forming the majority of basal diplodocines.
facts.quote: En 2012, durante una redescripción del taxón por Philip Mannion et al., se recuperó, en ambos cladogramas, por ser especie hermana de Supersaurus vivianae y juntas formando la mayoría de los diplodócinos basales.

facts.statement: A 2014 cladogram found the group compatible but determined Dinheirosaurus was more primitive than Apatosaurus and therefore outside Diplodocinae.
facts.quote: Sin embargo, un cladograma de 2014 encontró que su grupo era compatible, pero de hecho era más primitivo que Apatosaurus y por lo tanto fuera de Diplodocinae.

facts.statement: A 2004 study by Upchurch et al. classified Dinheirosaurus as an intermediate diplodocoid alongside Cetiosauriscus, Amphicoelias, and Losillasaurus.
facts.quote: Un estudio realizado en 2004 por Upchurch et al. encontró que Dinheirosaurus era un diplodocoide intermedio, junto con Cetiosauriscus, Amphicoelias y Losillasaurus.

facts.statement: Bonaparte and Mateus found that Dinheirosaurus possessed both derived characteristics compared to Diplodocus and plesiomorphic traits suggesting separate branching, concluding it is not a descendant of Diplodocus.
facts.quote: Bonaparte y Mateus encontraron que algunas de las características presentes sugerían que Dinheirosaurus era más derivado que Diplodocus, pero las características plesiomorfas presentes también concluyen que se ramificaron por separado y Dinheirosaurus no es descendiente de Diplodocus.

facts.statement: Dinheirosaurus lived during the Kimmeridgian stage, approximately 152.21 to 149.2 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Kimmeridgian to Kimmeridgian (152.21 to 149.2 million years ago)

facts.statement: Supersaurus lourinhanensis lived in the Lourinhã Formation during the Late Jurassic.
facts.quote: Supersaurus lourinhanensis fue uno de los muchos dinosaurios que vivieron en la formación Lourinhã durante el Jurásico tardío.

facts.statement: Sauropods were less common in the Lourinhã Formation, represented by the intermediate diplodocid Supersaurus lourinhanensis, the camarasaurid Lourinhasaurus alenquerensis, the turiasaurian Zby atlanticus, and the brachiosaurid Lusotitan.
facts.quote: Los saurópodos son menos comunes, con solo un diplodócido intermedio y Supersaurus lourinhanensis, el camarasáurido Lourinhasaurus alenquerensis, el turiasauriano Zby atlanticus y el braquiosáurido Lusotitan.

facts.statement: As a diplodocid, it is probable that Supersaurus lourinhanensis used its tail as a whip capable of supersonic speed.
facts.quote: Como diplodócido, es probable que Supersaurus lourinhanensis que su cola pudiera usarse como un látigo, con velocidad supersónica.

facts.statement: Related to Apatosaurus and Diplodocus, Dinheirosaurus likely possessed a square snout, indicating it was a non-selective ground herbivore.
facts.quote: Al estar relacionado con Apatosaurus y Diplodocus, Dinheirosaurus probablemente poseía un hocico cuadrado. Esto significa que probablemente fue un saurópodo no selectivo de alimentación en tierra.

facts.statement: Supersaurus lourinhanensis is one of the relatively few sauropods for which gastroliths were found associated with the type specimen.
facts.quote: Supersaurus lourinhanensis es uno de los relativamente pocos saurópodos para los cuales se encontraron gastrolitos junto con el espécimen tipo.

facts.statement: Because birds typically have gastroliths weighing 1.05% of their body mass, while Diplodocus had only 0.03%, researchers suggest Dinheirosaurus likely used gastroliths for mineral absorption rather than a bird-style gastric mill.
facts.quote: Debido a la gran cantidad de gastrolitos que se encuentran en las aves. Cuando se encontró que las aves tenían típicamente un 1,05% de sus gastrolitos de peso corporal, el saurópodo Diplodocus, que tenía la mayor cantidad de gastrolitos, solo poseía un 0,03% del peso corporal. Esto significa que dado que los otros saurópodos Dinheirosaurus y Cedarosaurus tenían menos gastrolitos, es poco probable que un molino gástrico de estilo aviar haya evolucionado en los saurópodos y en su lugar podrían haber utilizado gastrolitos para absorber minerales.

facts.statement: Many eusauropods, including Supersaurus lourinhanensis, have been found in Late Jurassic Europe.
facts.quote: Muchos eusaurópodos, incluido el Supersaurus lourinhanensis, se han encontrado en el Jurásico tardío de Europa.

facts.statement: The sauropods in the region date to around the base of the Tithonian, indicated by the presence of Anchispirocyclina lusitanica.
facts.quote: Los saurópodos son de alrededor de la base del titoniense, según la presencia de Anchispirocyclina lusitanica.

facts.statement: It is debated whether the biogeography of primitive sauropods is incomplete, with possible eusauropods and primitive diplodocids surviving in the Late Jurassic, potentially until the Berriasian.
facts.quote: Esto sugiere que la biogeografía de los saurópodos primitivos es incompleta, con posibles eusauropodos y diplodócidos primitivos que sobrevivieron en el Jurásico Tardío, potencialmente hasta el Berriasiense.
